name: Warning the User about the Changes in the Temperature and Humidity
description: Construct a program that receives the temperature and humidity for today and yesterday and warns the user when it is getting colder or warmer or neither. When it is getting warmer, the program should also warn the user about the changes in humidity. In particular, it should warn the user when today's humidity is more, less, or has not changed compared to yesterday's humidity. Note that the temperature and humidity values could have a decimal point.
code:
#Step 1: Read the temperature for today and yesterday
text = input("Enter the yesterday's temperature: ")
yesterday = float(text)
text = input("Enter the today's temperature: ")
today = float(text)  
#Step 2: Read the humidity for today and yesterday
text = input("Enter yesterday's humidity: ")
humidity_yesterday = float(text)
text = input("Enter today's humidity: ")
humidity_today = float(text)
#Step 3: Warn the user about the changes in the temperature
if today < yesterday :
    print("It is getting colder!")
else :
    if today > yesterday :
        #Step 3.1: Determine and warn the user about the changes in humidity when it is getting warmer
        if humidity_today < humidity_yesterday :
            print("It is getting warmer but less humid!")
        elif humidity_today > humidity_yesterday :
            print("It is getting warmer and more humid!")
        else :
            print("It is getting warmer but humidity has not changed!")
    else :
        print("Temperature is the same as yesterday!")

commentList: This line shows a prompt to the user and saves whatever they type into the variable text: input(...) displays the prompt string and returns the entered characters as a string, and the = operator assigns that string to text.
You should know input() always returns text (a string). It does not convert to a number for you — the conversion to float happens on the next line (yesterday = float(text)).

A common mistake is to assume input() gives a numeric value; if you try to compare or compute with text before converting, you will get wrong results or errors. Also, if the user types non-numeric text, the later float(...) call will raise a ValueError.

For a better user experience, you should make the prompt clearer and include units or an example (for example: "Enter yesterday's temperature (°C), e.g. 21.5: "). The current prompt text is awkwardly phrased ('the yesterday's'); remove the extra 'the'.

As a best practice, consider using a more descriptive variable name (e.g., yesterday_input or temp_yesterday_str), call .strip() to remove extra spaces, and wrap the float conversion in try/except to handle invalid input gracefully.
Remember that input() blocks program execution until the user presses Enter, so your program will wait here for the user to respond.

commentList: Purpose: this line shows the user the message 'It is getting colder!' — it is the visible warning for the branch where today's temperature is lower than yesterday's.

Common mistakes and errors: if you forget the quotes you'll get a NameError/SyntaxError; if you omit the parentheses in Python 3 you'll get a SyntaxError; wrong indentation or mixing tabs and spaces can cause IndentationError or change when the message prints.

Best practice suggestions: consider printing the actual values to make the message clearer, e.g. print(f"It is getting colder: today {today} < yesterday {yesterday}"), keep consistent indentation (4 spaces), and use meaningful messages or a logging system in larger programs.
